title: How would you build a tool that turns a PDF book into a voiced anime-style visual novel?
author: Beginning_Cable3649
selftext:
i’m trying to figure out how to build a program where I upload a PDF of a book and it generates a playable visual novel: anime-style art, consistent characters and settings, chapters, and voice acting that fits the setting (e.g. Latin or Roman-flavored English for ancient Rome, a UK accent for a British setting, Japanese for a story set in Japan). I’ve got a rough idea of the pipeline:

1. Parse the PDF and split it into chapters and scenes
   1. Use an LLM to extract the cast, settings, and character descriptions, then rewrite the prose as a VN script (narration, dialogue, expressions, backgrounds)
   2. Generate backgrounds and character sprites with an image model
   3. Generate voice lines with TTS
   4. Package it all in Ren’Py or a web player

Where I’m stuck and would love advice:

∙ Art consistency: What’s the best way to keep characters and locations looking the same across hundreds of images? LoRAs, IP-Adapter, reference sheets, something else?

∙ Voices: Which TTS options handle multiple accents and languages well, and give each character a distinct voice? Anything decent for Latin?

∙ Engine: Is Ren’Py the right choice, or is a custom web player easier to automate?

∙ Cost: Any tips for keeping image and voice costs manageable for a full-length novel?

∙ Long books: How do you keep an LLM consistent across a whole book without losing plot or character details? I’m planning to start with a short public-domain story from Project Gutenberg. Has anyone built something similar, or know of existing projects I should look at? Thanks!
